discussion_comments.comment_body: Callers pass the name of a field as a string: `"statusWriteQueue"` or `"compactionStateWriteQueue"`. The call site does not say what the string does, and the compiler accepts the wrong string. This is the problem with a boolean parameter, one step removed. Please pass the getter and setter for the queue instead, or give each queue its own small method over one shared body.
Done: `enqueueStatusWrite` and `enqueueCompactionStateWrite` each hand a getter/setter pair for their queue to one `chainWrite`. No strings.

Similar to feedback on your other PR, I suggest using a string union here instead of a boolean. Booleans often are not flexible enough to model what is going on, and tend to proliferate. Then you get a lot of booleans where a subset of the states are invalid and it gets confusing and hard to test.

In general, it is better if we can reflect the "only set for `beforeRun`" in a TypeScript shape which has `{foo: "beforeRun", entry: "run" | "continue", ...}` so the rest of the system can use these fields in a typesafe way. Also possible to lift a property out of an object by construction to relate these fields with some other state. (Does that make sense? TL;DR, can we use the type system here to communicate "only set for `beforeRun`" and benefit from checking?)

I am not a huge fan of boolean fields because often enough the domain isn't actually a boolean; can we describe what this situation is, and then use strings as an enum to explain "seeded" | "written" or whatever is actually happening here?

Even with only two values, the enum is still better because it describes what "not seeded" is in a positive way, not through negation.
